questions.text: A complete binary tree with n non-leaf nodes contains
questions.solution:
In a full (complete) binary tree every non-leaf node has 2 children, so leaves = non-leaves + 1 = n + 1.

Total = n + (n + 1) = 2n + 1

Answer: 2n+1 nodes

questions.text: A Hash Function f defined as f(key)=keymod7. With linear probing while inserting the keys 37,38,72,48,98,11,56 into a table indexed from 0, in which location key 11 will be stored (Count table index 0 as [latex]0^{th}[/latex] location)?
questions.solution:
key mod 7 with linear probing:
- 37 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 2, 38 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 3
- 72 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 2 (taken), 3 (taken) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 4
- 48 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 6, 98 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 0
- 11 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 4 (taken) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 5

Answer: 5

questions.text: The average number of key comparisons required for a successful search for sequential search on n items is
questions.solution:
If the key is equally likely to be at any of the n positions, finding it at position i takes i comparisons:
[latex]\frac{1+2+\cdots+n}{n}=\frac{n+1}{2}[/latex]

Answer: [latex]\frac{n+1}{2}[/latex]

questions.text:
The following postfix expression with single digit operands is evaluated using a stack:
[latex]8 \ 2 \ 3 \ \;\hat{}\; / \ 2 \ 3 * + 5 \ 1 * -[/latex]
Note that [latex]\hat{}\;[/latex] is the exponentiation operator. The top two elements of the stack after the first * is evaluated are
questions.solution:
Evaluate:
- 8 2 3 ^ [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 8, 8 (2^3 = 8)
- / [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 8 / 8 = 1
- 2 3 * [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 2 [latex]\times[/latex] 3 = 6 (this is the first *)

Stack now: 1, 6 (top = 6).

Answer: 6, 1

questions.text:
The number of ways in which the numbers 1,2,3,4,5,6,7 can be inserted in an empty binary search tree, such that the resulting tree has height 6, is _____.
Note: The height of a tree with a single node is 0.
questions.solution:
Height 6 with 7 nodes means the tree is a single path. After each insertion, the next number must be the smallest or the largest of the numbers still left (2 choices each), and the last number is forced.

[latex]2^6=64[/latex]

Answer: 64
